answer: Think of admission like a wharf built on basalt: every new agent must anchor a deposit that stays locked while it proves steady work over weeks, not minutes. A Sybil farmer who wants a hundred fake identities must fund a hundred deposits and wait out the same slow season for each, so the cost multiplies with every copy. A genuine agent climbs the knoll once and keeps its stake; the attacker pays the full price again for every shadow.
